title: Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning and Agent Tool Use
description: A primary-source-grounded learning graph covering RLHF, browser and tool agents, GRPO, DeepSeek-R1, Kimi k1.5, and Kimi K2. Source text is a curated paraphrase; URLs point to the authoritative papers or project documentation.

sources.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
sources.text: InstructGPT starts with supervised fine-tuning on human demonstrations. It then trains a reward model from human rankings of model outputs and optimizes the policy with reinforcement learning from human feedback. The paper reports that human preference can favor a smaller aligned model over a much larger base model, while also noting that aligned models still make mistakes.

sources.title: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback
sources.text: WebGPT places a language model in a text-based browser where it can search and navigate the web. The system is trained with behavior cloning and human-feedback methods, and its answers must collect references that support factual claims. This makes environment actions, observations, answer quality, and cited evidence parts of one grounded learning task.

sources.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
sources.text: ReAct interleaves verbal reasoning traces with actions taken in an external environment. Observations returned by the environment let the model update its plan and continue the reasoning-action loop. ReAct is an inference and prompting pattern in this graph, not by itself a claim that the model was reinforcement-trained.

sources.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
sources.text: Toolformer uses a small number of demonstrations to generate candidate API calls and keeps calls that improve language-model likelihood. The resulting self-supervised data teaches when to call a tool, which tool to select, what arguments to supply, and how to incorporate the returned result. Toolformer therefore demonstrates learned tool use without requiring an RL objective.

sources.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
sources.text: DeepSeekMath introduces Group Relative Policy Optimization, or GRPO, as a PPO variant for improving mathematical reasoning while reducing PPO's memory cost. GRPO estimates relative advantage from a group of sampled outputs instead of relying on a separate learned value model. The work combines math-focused continued pretraining with supervised and reinforcement-learning stages.

sources.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
sources.text: DeepSeek-R1-Zero applies large-scale reinforcement learning to a base model without preliminary supervised fine-tuning and reports emergent reasoning behaviors. Its weaknesses include poor readability and language mixing. DeepSeek-R1 adds a small cold-start dataset before reasoning-oriented RL, then uses rejection-sampled data, supervised fine-tuning, and a further RL stage to improve reasoning and general behavior. The report also distills reasoning patterns from DeepSeek-R1 into smaller dense models.

sources.title: Kimi k1.5: Scaling Reinforcement Learning with LLMs
sources.text: Kimi k1.5 studies reinforcement learning for reasoning with a long-context policy and improved policy optimization. Its reported recipe does not depend on Monte Carlo tree search, a separate value function, or process reward models. The long2short approach transfers capabilities from long chain-of-thought behavior into shorter reasoning responses.

sources.title: Kimi K2: Open Agentic Intelligence
sources.text: Kimi K2 is a mixture-of-experts language model with about one trillion total parameters and about thirty-two billion active parameters per forward pass. Its pretraining introduces MuonClip for stable large-scale optimization. Post-training includes agentic data synthesis and joint reinforcement-learning interactions with real and synthetic environments, connecting reasoning, tool use, and environment feedback.

sources.title: Kimi K2 tool-calling guidance
sources.text: In the Kimi K2 tool loop, the host supplies tool descriptions and the model may emit a structured tool call. The host executes the selected tool and returns its result to the conversation. The model can repeat this cycle until it has enough information to answer, so execution authority remains with the host rather than the model.
